one_month_reasoning: Only one scheduled company event falls in the window: Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-20 after the close [2]. Consensus is about $2.64-2.69 non-GAAP EPS on about $2.91-2.96B revenue [5]. Three things make the print harder than the beat streak suggests. (1) The comp is tough: Q3 2025 procedures grew about 19% [44], and guidance toward the 14.5% midpoint implies roughly 13-14% in H2 [19]. (2) This is the first time management will size the Extended Use Program, which it called 'directionally similar to 2020' [42]. The 2020 program was modeled at about 6.6% of I&A [43]. Force-feedback, stapling and energy instruments are excluded this time [37], so I expect a guide equal to about a 1-3% 2027 I&A/procedure drag. A number above 3% would be the negative surprise. (3) U.S. demand: HCA's 10-Q shows exchange admissions -15% and outpatient surgeries -3.4% [41]. Macro is a new headwind I missed in round 1. The 10-year rose from 4.79% to 5.29% during September (FRED [32]) after the 2026-09-16 Fed hike [39]. That pressures long-duration medtech multiples inside the window, though yields eased on Oct 1. On the other side: four straight EPS beats [1], and the stock has rallied about 15% off mid-September lows [21]. Net: median about $400 (flat), sigma about 11% (the 37%/3.5 = 10.6% baseline, widened for the earnings gap), with a slightly fatter left tail for the EUP sizing and rates. I do not use own-history Q3 report-day base rates (small sample, per supervisor).

fair_value.method: Three-method blend, each net of a $5/share litigation EV haircut. Forward P/E: FY2028 non-GAAP EPS $13.5 x 30.5 = $412, less $5 = $407 (weight 0.5). EV/sales: FY2028 revenue $14.81B x 9.25x plus $9.5B net cash, over 355M shares, less $5 = $408 (weight 0.25). FCF yield: 2028 FCF $5.24B at a 3.8% EV yield plus net cash, less $5 = $410 (weight 0.25). Blended fair value about $409, 2% above the $401.24 close. Down from $424 mainly because the 10-year is at 5.29%.

bear.story: U.S. procedure growth slides to 9-10% as HCA-style coverage attrition [41] extends into 2027 Medicaid work requirements [26] and bariatrics keep shrinking [28]. The EUP is sized above 3% of I&A/procedure and front-loaded into 2027 [42][43]. Hospital capex stays tight (41% of systems cutting [33]), slowing placements. The class trial in Sept 2027 goes badly after the SIS reversal [40]. Rates stay above 5% [32]. FY2028 EPS about $12.4 at about 23x.

base.story: Procedures grow 12-14%. Robotic share in general surgery is still climbing (robotic chole about 31% of laparoscopic-plus-robotic cases, rising fast in high-BMI patients [34]; hernia [35]). dV5 upgrades, Ion and SP indications keep revenue growing about 12-13% [20]. EUP drag about 2% of I&A [37][42]. Ottava stays at select customers, with no commercial sites publicised since authorization [38][25]. FY2028 EPS $13.5 at about 30.5x, less litigation.

bull.story: The EUP is sized at the low end (~1%) and lifts benign-procedure volume. U.S. growth holds around 13% despite coverage losses, showing share gain from laparoscopy [34][35]. Remanufacturing stays marginal (still four Restore clearances [36]). Yields retreat from 5.3% [32]. EPS about $14.4 and the multiple recovers to about 37x.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $300 (9% under the $328.57 52-week low, about 22x my FY2028 EPS, about 25x the FY2027 consensus), the price would mean a structural break rather than rates or sentiment. That would be one of: U.S. da Vinci procedure growth in single digits (a 2027 guide below about 11%), an EUP sized well above 3% of I&A/procedure or front-loaded into 2027, an adverse turn in the hospital antitrust class case (trial 2027-09-14) after the Ninth Circuit SIS reversal [40], or visible share loss to Ottava/Hugo. A rates-driven de-rating alone would more likely stop around $330-350. That is why I keep the break at $300 even though my fair value fell.

key_uncertainties: EUP sizing on 2026-10-20: the plausible range is a 1-3% I&A/procedure drag in 2027 [42][43][37]. The 2020 'realised -2%' precedent is single-sourced and COVID-distorted.
Rates: the 10-year rose 50bp in September to 5.29% [32]. If it holds, 30x may still be generous. If it reverses, the bull case gains.
U.S. procedure growth vs coverage attrition (HCA uninsured admissions +23.4%, outpatient surgeries -3.4% [41]) and 2027 Medicaid work requirements [26].
Ottava/Hugo pace. I found no publicised Ottava commercial sites since the 2026-07-22 authorization [38]. That fits a capacity-limited launch, but it is absence of evidence, not data.
Hospital antitrust class trial (2027-09-14), strengthened by the SIS reversal [40]: a left-tail item.
Remanufacturing adoption: four Restore clearances plus older Rebotix/Iconocare ones [36][29]. Volume is not observable.
Hospital capex: survey shows more systems cutting than increasing and a strong ROI focus [33]. That could slow system placements while favouring procedure-ROI arguments.
reasoning: Round 2. I took the supervisor's findings as given where they had evidence: the HCA 10-Q figures (uninsured admissions +23.4%, exchange -15%, outpatient surgeries -3.4%) [41]; the EUP is 'directionally similar to 2020' and sizing comes Oct 20 [42], with the 2020 program modeled at about 6.6% of I&A [43], giving a 1-3% drag range; the Ninth Circuit SIS reversal with the class trial on 2027-09-14 [40]; Ottava cleared on 2026-07-22 with a select-customer launch [38]; the Fed hiked on 2026-09-16 [39]; and Q3 2025's 19% procedure comp [44]. On the source critique: the supervisor said my round-1 alternative sources were mostly newsletter opinion, so I dropped the newsletter price targets (TIKR $585 and others) as inputs entirely and spent about 9 searches/fetches on actual data. (a) FRED DGS10 [32]: the 10-year ran from 4.79% (Sep 1) to 5.29% (Sep 30). The supervisor could only confirm ~5.01% on Sep 16. The primary series shows the move kept going, which is the main reason my multiple is 30.5x, not the supervisor's 31-32x. (b) Claims and registry data on robotic penetration: robotic chole at 31% of the laparoscopic-plus-robotic mix and 56% in BMI>=50 patients by 2024 [34]; inguinal hernia 0.7% to 28.8% in a Michigan registry [35] (dated). The runway in benign general surgery, the very segment the EUP targets, is still large, which supports the base case's 12-14% procedures. (c) Hospital capex survey (Sage Growth via HFMA [33]): 41% of systems cutting vs 31% increasing, with ROI the top criterion. Mildly negative for placements. (d) FDA remanufacturing: no new Restore clearances since March 2026 (four total) [36], so the threat is not accelerating. (e) Ottava: no publicised commercial sites after authorization [38], consistent with the capacity limit [25]. (f) EUP scope excludes force-feedback, stapling and energy [37], which caps the drag. Valuation: FY2028 EPS $13.5 (round 1: $13.6); P/E $407, EV/sales $408, FCF yield $410, all net of $5 litigation. Blended fair value $409 (round 1: $424). I am below the supervisor's ~$420 only because of the rate data. Scenarios $285/$415/$550 at 25/50/25, mean about $416. Ladder: lognormal mixture (70% sigma 0.28, 30% sigma 0.45 with slight negative skew) around a $401 median, mean about $420. P(>=401) = 0.49 (round 1: 0.52; supervisor: 0.54). The consensus target of about $476-482 [5] is near my 65th percentile. I treat it as lagging evidence. X and Reddit were again not useful or reachable, and there is no prediction market on ISRG-specific events.
